questions.q: What problem does workload identity solve?
options: It speeds up container image builds
It lets a workload authenticate to cloud APIs without a stored long-lived credential
It replaces Kubernetes RBAC entirely
It encrypts network traffic between pods
questions.explain: Workload identity lets a pod obtain cloud credentials through a short-lived, federated token instead of storing a long-lived secret or access key.

questions.q: Before workload identity, what were the two realistic ways a pod could get cloud API access?
options: A stored secret in a Kubernetes Secret, or a credential baked into the container image
A QR code and a biometric scan
Kubernetes RBAC alone, with no cloud credential needed
A shared cluster-wide password
questions.explain: Both options involved a long-lived credential sitting somewhere — in a Kubernetes Secret object or baked into an image layer — which is exactly the standing-secret risk workload identity avoids.

questions.q: In federated identity, what does the cloud provider actually trust?
options: A password shared out of band
Tokens issued by the Kubernetes cluster's own OIDC issuer for a specific service account
Any token presented by any pod in the cluster
A certificate stored permanently in the pod's image
questions.explain: The cloud provider is configured to trust tokens from the cluster's OIDC issuer, scoped to a specific, narrowly-defined service account — not just any token from any pod.

questions.q: What is AWS IRSA the equivalent of in Azure?
options: Azure Key Vault
Azure Workload Identity
Azure RBAC role assignments
Microsoft Entra ID Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explain: AWS IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) and Azure Workload Identity are the two cloud-specific implementations of the same federated-identity pattern.

questions.q: How does Northbridge Retail's checkout pod authenticate to Azure Key Vault under this model?
options: By storing the Key Vault access key in a Kubernetes Secret
Through a federated service account with a token exchanged for credentials scoped to one Key Vault role — no stored credential at all
By using the cluster administrator's personal login
By embedding the secret directly in the application's source code
questions.explain: The checkout pod's service account is federated to an Entra ID application holding exactly the Key Vault Secrets User role scoped to one vault, with no long-lived credential stored anywhere.
